frase_inicial: Michael: your cash, the planned home and your retirement all collide in January 2027

tarjetas.frente: January 2027 home and vacation strain your cash
tarjetas.reverso: If you set aside the home payment and the trip from the cash you now hold, you would have no liquid cushion left. That makes any pay cut, job gap or bill harder to absorb and risks selling investments at a bad time.
tarjetas.detalle: Assumes $113,300 needed for the home and $3,500 for the vacation in January 2027; accessible cash today $30,000.

tarjetas.frente: Retirement at 58 currently leaves money short later in life
tarjetas.reverso: Your plan expects savings to run out before the end of your life plan. That means planned spending would be unpaid unless you change how much you save, when you retire, or how you spend in retirement.
tarjetas.detalle: Savings projected to run out at age 85; retirement gap about $1,177,586 in today's dollars.

tarjetas.frente: Life and liability protection is thin for a single earner
tarjetas.reverso: If something happened to you, the coverage in place would not replace your income or protect the assets you’ve built. Fixing this costs premiums and competes with cash and saving choices.
tarjetas.detalle: Life insurance on file $180,000; recommended minimum range $900,000 to $1,800,000; no umbrella policy recorded.

tarjetas.frente: High-interest credit card is the most expensive debt
tarjetas.reverso: That card eats money in interest each month. Paying it faster reduces interest paid but uses cash that you might need for the home or your emergency cushion. It's a clear tradeoff.
tarjetas.detalle: Card balance $3,500 at 20% APR, monthly payment $200, projected payoff July 2028.

tarjetas.frente: Your invested mix and home plan pull in different directions
tarjetas.reverso: You aim for a growth mix for long-term gains, but the money for the home is short-term. Selling investments for the down payment lowers the base that funds retirement and raises the odds you’ll change the retirement timeline.
tarjetas.detalle: Invested book $145,000; suggested shift of about $19,900 toward higher growth in plan moves.

movimientos.title: Add umbrella cover
movimientos.action: Add $1M of umbrella to raise the liability shield

movimientos.title: Lower the withdrawal rate
movimientos.action: Cutting withdrawals to $10,300/year (6.0%) reaches the sustainable band

movimientos.title: Raise growth allocation toward glide
movimientos.action: Move the invested mix from 74% to 88% growth (glide 98%) for the next horizon-fit band — about $19,900 of the invested book

mapa.aviso: Illustrative simulator: it shows the direction of change, not a Sherpas projection.

siguiente_paso.razon: Because there is no umbrella recorded and a claim could reach your liquid assets and net worth, adding liability cover is the fastest way to protect what you already have without touching the down payment plans yet.
pasos: Call your current auto or renter insurer or agent and ask whether an umbrella policy can be added to your account
If yes, get a written quote for a one million dollar liability policy and note the premium
Compare that premium to your monthly budget and decide whether to buy it now or delay until after you confirm the home cash plan
